id_and_class.theory_title: Gabriel’s New Realism and Field of Sense
id_and_class.summary: Markus Gabriel holds that consciousness cannot be reduced to brain states: the brain is necessary for it but neither sufficient nor identical with it. Drawing on his New Realism and ontological pluralism, he treats consciousness as tied to ‘fields of sense’, the contexts in which the world appears and becomes meaningful, and as the space where freedom, value, and responsibility show up.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as the Condition of Meaning and Freedom

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is no substance or object of science like a molecule. It is the precondition for fields of sense, the ways in which things appear and have meaning.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: The brain is a necessary condition for consciousness but not a sufficient one, and not identical with it. Gabriel calls the idea that we are our brains ‘one of the most dangerous ideologies of our time’.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Unclear: Gabriel says mental phenomena emerge in culturally infused fields, yet also treats consciousness as the precondition of all fields of sense.
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Consciousness is intentional and normative: conscious beings are aware of how things are and of how they ought to be, and they interpret, evaluate, and create norms.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: A plurality of fields of sense as distinct ontological domains; free agents; norms and values as real.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Through philosophical, phenomenological, and normative analysis. Treating consciousness as a thing fully explained by natural science is a category error.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Fields of sense: contexts in which objects appear and acquire meaning, with consciousness as their condition.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Self and personhood; intentionality; freedom and agency; meaning and value
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: The field of sense. Things exist and become intelligible only as they appear within some field, and consciousness is what makes such appearing possible.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Not located in the brain; Gabriel insists consciousness is not a thing with a place.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Consciousness is the seat of freedom. Gabriel argues that reconciling free will with physical contingency requires rejecting a strictly naturalistic, deterministic, physicalist framework.
core_claims_and_evidence: Neurocentrism, the view that being a mental being is nothing but having a suitable brain, mistakes a necessary condition for the whole story.
Consciousness is not an object of science in the way atoms are, so reducing it to neuronal activity is a category error.
Normative, semantic, and existential aspects of mind cannot be captured by empirical science alone.
Consciousness is bound up with ethical life and self-understanding, as the space where value and responsibility appear.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical: ontology, phenomenology, and normative argument.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Calling consciousness both a field of sense and the precondition of all fields of sense leaves its status unsettled, as does saying mental phenomena emerge in those fields.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Gabriel offers no account of how the brain, as a necessary condition, contributes to consciousness, and none of phenomenal feel.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Fits his ontological pluralism, and the phenomenological orientation aligns him with Husserl and Heidegger against materialist philosophy of mind.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Gabriel calls the brain a necessary condition for consciousness, so his view gives no basis for consciousness continuing after it.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Meaning, freedom, and value appear in conscious, norm-making life; Gabriel invokes no cosmic purpose.

sources_and_references.title_with_names: Gabriel’s New Realism and Field of Sense (Landscape of Consciousness entry), Markus Gabriel
